newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia close to contracting parliament travel.
newsitem.headline: Australia close to contracting parliament travel.

text.p: Australian Administrative Services Minister David Jull said on Monday he expected to sign a contract this week to privatise the administration of parliamentary travel.
"I'm pretty confident we will get it signed this week," Jull told reporters after a speech on contracting out government services to small business.
He said the parliamentary travel business is worth A$16.8 million a year and the government hoped to save at least A$1.5 million a year by contracting it out to the private sector.
The government currently handles the travel arrangements for parliament's 224 members, their staff and parliamentary public servants.
Prime Minister John Howard's conservative Liberal-National government has progressively privatised some government services and business units since winning office in March 1996.
Public disquiet over parliamentary travel arrangements has also increased after allegations of travel fraud against some current and former politicians.
Two sitting parliamentarians and two former members have been charged with fraud. They have denied any wrongdoing.
